_what_changed: The replication is DONE: ten of twelve families measured, zero beat a no-skill size
control. That phase was pre-registered as a diagnostic, not a search, and it stayed one.
The owner has now explicitly directed a SEARCH on BRAIN with the goal of a submission.
That is a different activity under different rules and it is recorded as such here
rather than allowed to blur into the diagnostic's record.
_submission_note: Authorization for an actual BRAIN submission is a separate, explicit owner decision, made after a candidate clears the bars below. Nothing in this file authorizes one.

the_bar.primary: decile monotonicity must EXCEED control_size, not 0.5
_why: group_rank(assets, sector) -- ranking companies by total assets, no skill in it --
orders its deciles at +0.867 market-neutral on 10/10 clean deciles. Four of the ten
families measured clear the declared 0.5 bar and ALL FOUR clear it by roughly the
margin the control does. The highest, sales_yield at +0.988, is the most mechanically
size-linked construction in the set. Scoring against 0.5 rediscovers size; scoring
also_required: middle-8 monotonicity clears too, in the same direction (extremes-only is concentration)
the de-sized variant survives -- a signal whose edge vanishes once size is ranked out was size
the de-sizing method is itself validated: a de-sized control_size must go FLAT
density: the underlying fields at >= 0.5 coverage, and 1.0 preferred
explicitly_NOT_the_bar: BRAIN Sharpe >= 1.25 and fitness >= 1.0. `growth` clears both and returns LESS than
the no-skill control (8.35% vs 8.57%). The scoreboard is the instrument that produced
eleven years of headline numbers here that all died.

sign_discipline._note: Every candidate's sign is declared with the expression, before its ladder runs. A negative result is a refutation, not a discovery with the sign flipped. Held for Form 4 (Step 286) and FINRA short volume (Step 282); held for balance_sheet_quality here at -0.927; holds for anything found now.

_honest_limit: BRAIN cannot count its own multiple testing and neither can we. Unlimited simulations,
a fixed in-sample window shared by every user, and circulated templates. fundamental6
has 86,751 users; pv1 has 90,051. Anything found on those is the survivor of a search
whose size is not merely uncounted but uncountable. A pass here is therefore WEAKER
evidence than a pass on our own data, not stronger, and must be described that way.
This is why the search targets the least-trodden datasets available.

why_sentiment_first: coverage 1.0 rather than the fundamentals' 0.5, which removes the binding density caveat
on every number the diagnostic produced
socialmedia8 has 6,299 users and news18 8,996, against fundamental6's 86,751
a z-scored sentiment level is structurally far less size-linked than a ratio whose
denominator IS market cap -- sales_yield at +0.988 shows how easily that recovers size

what_a_pass_would_and_would_not_mean.would_mean: a hypothesis worth rebuilding and retesting on OUR panel, under its own pre-registration
would_not_mean: a tradeable strategy -- BRAIN's data never leaves the platform (verified: no export
endpoint at any level, /data-fields/{id}/data and /data-sets/{id}/export both 404)
anything about our books, which are weekly long-only top-5..20 against BRAIN's
satisfaction of the cost gate -- BRAIN returns appear gross; 0/10/50/100bps stays ours

kill_conditions: de-sized control_size does NOT go flat -> the de-sizing method is broken, nothing readable
a candidate's edge disappears when de-sized -> it was size, record and close it
monotonicity below control_size -> not a candidate, whatever its Sharpe
field coverage below 0.5 -> not measurable on deciles at all
